`scripts/backup.sh --dry-run SOURCE DEST` now prints each file and directory it would copy as a `source -> destination` line and exits without creating the dated folder or copying anything. I ran it against a scratch directory: the dry run left DEST untouched, a missing SOURCE exits non-zero, and the normal copy still works.

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# backup.sh [--dry-run] SOURCE DEST: copy SOURCE into DEST/<date>/
set -eu
dry=
if [ "${1:-}" = --dry-run ]; then
    dry=1
    shift
fi
src=${1:?usage: backup.sh [--dry-run] SOURCE DEST}
dest=${2:?usage: backup.sh [--dry-run] SOURCE DEST}
target=$dest/$(date +%F)
if [ -n "$dry" ]; then
    cd "$src"
    find . ! -name . | while IFS= read -r f; do
        echo "$src/${f#./} -> $target/${f#./}"
    done
    echo "dry run: nothing copied from $src to $target"
    exit 0
fi
mkdir -p "$target"
cp -R "$src/." "$target/"
echo "backed up $src to $target"
```

The README's Backup section now shows the `[--dry-run]` usage and describes the option in place of "Options: none".

`--dry-run` must come before SOURCE; accepting it in any position would need a real option loop.
I left the version at 1.3.2, since bumping means changing `VERSION`, `app/__init__.py`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` together; say so if this should ship as a release.
